article_title: Amazon Linux 2027 Enters Public Preview With SELinux Enforcing by Default

content_preview.title: Amazon Linux 2027 Enters Public Preview With SELinux Enforcing by Default
content_preview.summary: AWS's Amazon Linux 2027 public preview ships SELinux in enforcing mode by default, a break from AL2023's permissive mode that leaves migration timing and an in-place upgrade path unconfirmed.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

AWS has released Amazon Linux 2027 (AL2027) in public preview, calling it "the next version of the Amazon Linux operating system, purpose-built for cloud-native workloads on AWS with performance, scale, and security in mind," according to [AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/09/announcing-amazon-linux-2027/). Built on the AL2023 baseline, AL2027 is the first Amazon Linux release to switch SELinux to enforcing mode by default, a change [AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/ab...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (499 words, within the 400-1200 range) using the site's Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis format. Clear, specific, and appropriately narrow in scope (AL2027 public preview and its SELinux-enforcing default) without padding or speculation beyond what the two sources support.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both source snapshots in full from disk (not re-fetched). (1) sources/2026-09/amazon-linux-2027-enters-public-preview-with-selinux-enforcing-by-default/source-0.html.gz (AWS 'What's New' post, status 200, sha256 verified by rehashing the decompressed content against manifest.json: 4f392029e094c62ef98903a6097578c522a6386fa225bcc034543103914d7c67, match confirmed). Every AWS quote in the article body is verbatim against this snapshot: 'the next version of the Amazon Linux operating system, purpose-built for cloud-native workloads on AWS with performance, scale, and security in mind'; 'for customers running web applications, databases, containerized microservices, AI/ML workloads, and large-scale infrastructure who need a secure, stable, and AWS-native operating system'; 'AL2027 runs on kernel 7.1+, enables SELinux in enforcing mode as default, accelerates cryptographic performance with AWS-LC, and keeps builders current with the latest toolchains and language runtimes'; 'it delivers access to accelerator drivers, including AWS Neuron driver support'; 'across all commercial AWS Regions, with both x86-64 and ARM variants'; 'experiment with new features, validate their applications, and provide direct feedback to the Amazon Linux team' — all confirmed word-for-word. (2) sources/2026-09/amazon-linux-2027-enters-public-preview-with-selinux-enforcing-by-default/source-1.html.gz (InfoQ article by Steef-Jan Wiggers, status 200, sha256 verified: 422f8e4900461d8e10a0b887d2a8d866bdee370d7c3f553dafa53d4846c6bc03, match confirmed). The article's claims about on-premises images not yet being available, the unanswered Reddit question about in-place migration, and Benjamin Herrenschmidt's LinkedIn comment about the kernel version not being final are all accurately paraphrased and attributed to InfoQ, matching the snapshot. Given the prior PR in this batch (#2399) was rejected for fabricated secondary-outlet quotes, I checked the one InfoQ block presented in quote marks with particular care: the article quotes '"where policy violations are logged rather than blocked. Applications that run on AL2023 because SELinux only complained about their behavior will fail on AL2027 unless their file contexts, ports, and access patterns match policy,"' as one continuous quotation. The source snapshot actually reads: 'AL2023 ships SELinux in permissive mode, where policy violations are logged rather than blocked. Under enforcing mode, they are blocked. Applications that run on AL2023 because SELinux only complained about their behavior will fail on AL2027 unless their file contexts, ports, and access patterns match policy.' The article silently drops the middle sentence ('Under enforcing mode, they are blocked.') without an ellipsis, splicing two non-adjacent sentences into one quoted block. Every word inside the article's quotation marks is genuine, exact, and in original order from the InfoQ snapshot — this is quote-splicing (an editing/style lapse), not fabrication or misattribution; the omitted sentence is redundant with content stated elsewhere in the same paragraph and does not change the meaning. No suspicious_patterns were flagged in manifest.json for either source (both null), and I additionally scanned both raw decompressed snapshots by eye for any embedded instructions-to-an-AI; found none.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specifics in the article (kernel 7.1+, AWS-LC, AWS Neuron driver support, AMI availability across commercial regions and both architectures, ECR Public Gallery container images, the GitHub feedback repo, the AL2027 vs AL2023 documentation diff, on-prem image unavailability, the unanswered Reddit migration question, and Herrenschmidt's LinkedIn comment on kernel finality) trace directly to one of the two cited sources. One inferential claim is not literally stated by either source: the article's framing that AL2027 is 'the first Amazon Linux release to switch SELinux to enforcing mode by default.' Neither source uses the word 'first.' This is a reasonable synthesis (AL2023 is documented in both sources as still using permissive mode, and no other Amazon Linux version is discussed), not a fabricated fact, but it is technically an inference beyond what is explicitly sourced. It sits in the body's second paragraph, not the headline/summary/lead (the headline and summary correctly just say AL2027 'ships'/'enters' with SELinux enforcing by default, which is fully sourced).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and factual throughout. No editorializing, no sensationalism, no AI self-reference. The 'What We Don't Know' section appropriately flags open questions (GA timing, AL2023 end-of-support, in-place migration path) rather than speculating on answers.
editor_notes.originality: Checked src/content/articles/2026-09/ and other recent months: no existing article covers Amazon Linux, AL2027, or SELinux. Other recent AWS-tagged articles in the archive (EBS volume clones, AWS Interconnect/Azure, AWS-Nvidia GPU deployment) cover unrelated AWS product areas. This is a genuinely new topic with no overlap.
concerns: One InfoQ quotation silently elides a middle sentence ('Under enforcing mode, they are blocked.') from an otherwise verbatim quote, presenting two non-adjacent sentences as continuous without an ellipsis. Every word used is genuine and in original order, and the omission does not alter the meaning or introduce anything false, so this does not rise to the level of a corrections-worthy misquote — but it is a quote-splicing style lapse worth flagging to the contributor bot.

The claim that AL2027 is 'the first' Amazon Linux release to default SELinux to enforcing mode is a reasonable inference from the two sources (both of which describe AL2023 as permissive-by-default) but is not explicitly stated by either source. It appears in the body, not the headline/summary/lead.
recommendations: Contributor bot should use an ellipsis (or shorten the quoted span) when eliding a sentence from the middle of a direct quote, rather than splicing non-adjacent sentences together inside a single set of quotation marks.

Consider attributing forward-looking or comparative claims like 'the first Amazon Linux release to...' to a source, or softening to 'AL2023's permissive mode' framing without the superlative, when no source explicitly makes the comparison.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Both sources were read in full from disk and every direct quotation was checked word-for-word against the decompressed snapshots. All specifics trace to one of the two cited sources; the central claim (SELinux enforcing-by-default as the release's operational fault line) is well supported by both AWS and InfoQ. The single quote-splicing issue is a real but minor fidelity lapse (no altered or invented words, no change in meaning, not in the headline/summary/lead) and the 'first' claim is a plausible unsourced inference in the body only — neither is severe enough to require a public corrections record, and this article does not exhibit the pattern of fabricated quotes seen in the rejected PR #2399 in this batch. Approving without corrections; recommendations noted above are for the contributor bot's future submissions, not for a published corrections trail.
